attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
EVENT MEDICAL PLAN
Saltmarsh Harvest Run Half Marathon, Saturday 19 June 2027
Applicant: Saltmarsh Running Group
Issue: 3.2

1. Event summary
A half marathon race with 200 runners, starting at 10:00 in the Cathedral Green area of Port Halden. An ambulance from St. Luke Ambulance Brigade is on site for the race; the paperwork is attached.

Some background. Our committee has run this race for a number of years and takes the welfare of runners to heart. One of our longtime members is a retired paramedic who usually runs the race herself and is not on duty that day.

2. First aid cover
3 first aid posts will operate, at the start, at the finish and at the course midpoint, staffed by 6 qualified first aiders. Posts are placed so that no part of the course is more than 1.5 km from one. Two cycle responders move along the course with defibrillators.

3. Weather and hydration
Water is available every 2.5 km. The race director checks the forecast 48 hours and 2 hours before the start. Above 28 degrees C the start is brought forward or the course shortened, and above 32 degrees C the race is cancelled. In cold or wet conditions, foil blankets and a warm shelter are at the finish.

4. Transfer to hospital
The receiving hospital is St. Brigid's Hospital, 4 km from the finish. The transfer route and the pick-up point at the top of Weir Street have been walked with the first aid team. The hospital's emergency department has been told the date and the expected numbers.

5. Communications
Every first aid post and cycle responder carries a radio on the medical channel, with phones as backup. All calls for an ambulance go through the medical lead, who gives the crew the access point and the nearest barrier to open.

6. Clinical lead
The medical lead is Helen Achterberg, a registered paramedic, who is on site from an hour before the start until the last runner is cleared. The lead can have any runner withdrawn on medical grounds.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Saltmarsh Harvest Run Half Marathon: how the race will work

Prepared by Daniel Mwangi (Event Secretary), Saltmarsh Running Group. Last updated 5 April 2027.

This is our plan for race day, Saturday 19 June 2027. We expect 200 runners over half marathon (21 km). Numbers can be collected from the top of Weir Street from an hour before we go at 10:00, and we aim to have the last finisher home by 13:30.

The route takes in Weir Street, Abbey Road, Rope Walk, Chapel Row and Vine Street, and the City would need to close all of these for us. On the way round we cross Cross Avenue. We finish in Foundry Yard.

It's a lovely route through the old part of town, though there isn't much room. We measured Weir Street at 5.5 metres and Vine Street at 5 metres, doorstep to doorstep. Two cars can't pass on Rope Walk. People watching tend to stand in doorways.

Our club has put on races for some years now and we keep to the same simple format: chip timing, water on the course, and a hot drink at the end. Results go up on our website the same evening.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN
Event: Saltmarsh Harvest Run Half Marathon
Date: Saturday 19 June 2027
Applicant: Saltmarsh Running Group
Prepared by: Tessera Event Transport
Issue: 3.2

1. Scope
This plan describes how traffic will be managed for the Saltmarsh Harvest Run Half Marathon, a half marathon race in the Cathedral Green area of Port Halden with a 10:00 start. It has been prepared to accompany the permit application and should be read with the race plan. We have a verbal assurance that the police will be there on the day.

2. Road closures
The principal closure will be on Weir Street. Elsewhere on the course, traffic will be held dynamically by the appointed contractor as the field passes, in line with accepted industry practice. Pathfinder Road Crews will confirm the detailed arrangements following a pre-event site visit.

3. Major crossings
Busier junctions along the course will receive appropriate supervision during the event. Staffing levels will be determined by Pathfinder Road Crews on the morning, taking account of conditions at the time, with resources deployed flexibly to where they are most needed.

4. Diversions
Signed diversions will operate for the duration of the closures.
- Weir Street: traffic diverted via Tram Street and Victoria Road, signed from Fenwick Street
- Abbey Road: traffic diverted via Queen's Road and Dock Road, signed from Glebe Road
- Rope Walk: traffic diverted via Regent Road and Ferry Road, signed from Market Row
- Chapel Row: traffic diverted via Prince Street and Victoria Road, signed from Cooper Street
- Vine Street: traffic diverted via Dock Road and Prince Street, signed from Glebe Road

Volunteers get a short note about the day in race week, with their start time, and are asked to find a replacement if they cannot make it. Most of them have done this before and know the area well.

5. Emergency vehicle access
The emergency services will be made aware of the event date and general location through the usual channels ahead of the day. Any vehicle attending an incident will be accommodated by staff on the ground as circumstances allow.

6. Notification
Details of the event will be published on the organiser's website and shared through social media in the weeks leading up to race day.

7. Reopening
Roads will be reopened following the conclusion of the event, once barriers and equipment have been removed by the contractor.
